content.comment_body: Hello! I'm facing an unusual situation. There's a [product_name] device connected to our company network. Sometimes it's reachable and responds to PING commands, but it suddenly disconnects. I've verified the cables and network settings (IP, mask, gateway), and all seem fine. When I connect my notebook directly to the [product_name], I can PING it without issues. Can anyone assist?

Sorry, but this appears to be a network issue rather than a [product_name] problem. Without detailed network information, it's challenging to troubleshoot further. Since it's within a company network, you should coordinate with your network administrator. [user_name]

I've already consulted the network administrator, who checked everything and confirmed all is okay, including the cabling. What's puzzling is that connecting my notebook to the same network as the [product_name] and the company lets the [product_name] respond to PING. The device seems to 'wake up' with the notebook present, though I can't quite explain it. It stays connected for a few days before communication ends unexpectedly, and I have to reconnect the notebook to restore it.
Could you specify which [product_name] model you're referring to? Please provide the exact [article_no] and firmware [version_no].

There are many possible causes, making it difficult to narrow down from a distance. I personally don't think the issue is directly with the [product_name]. It seems more likely that the network switch puts the device connection into sleep mode when no data is being transmitted, only waking it upon a direct PC request. As mentioned earlier, we lack full details of the project and network setup. Regards, [user_name] (translated with Google)

I've verified with the network administrator that no switch configuration puts the [product_name] to sleep. I suspect the opposite could occur, with the [product_name] entering standby when there is no data flow.

I can't confirm if the opposite is true either. In my experience, only [product_name] units communicate actively within their dedicated network and tend to be quite communicative. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users report intermittent connectivity issues with a [product_name] device on a company network. While direct connections enable communication and PING responses, the device occasionally becomes unreachable after inactivity on the main network. Even after confirming cabling and network infrastructure are functioning, the problem persists, suggesting possible standby or sleep behavior related to either network switches or the device itself. Users are frustrated by the unpredictable nature of the connection loss, which occurs without apparent network changes.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the [product_name] device to be reliably accessible and responsive on the network at all times, without requiring manual intervention to restore communication. Continuous remote connectivity and stable network presence are anticipated.
